name: Helix Biosystems Cortical Depth Index
description:
The Cortical Depth Index is a distributed cranial BCI system consisting of a thin-film electrode mesh draped across the cortical surface through a keyhole surgical approach, paired with a subdermal processing cluster at the temporal bone. Its primary function is continuous cognitive performance indexing — the device maps the user's real-time neural activity patterns against Helix Biosystems' proprietary 'Depth Scoring' model, which purports to quantify executive function, working memory load, pattern recognition speed, and decision-making quality into a single rolling numerical score accessible to the user through a heads-up display or haptic feedback pulse. Helix markets the CDI as the definitive tool for cognitive self-optimization, sold through a subscription model that includes access to their proprietary coaching AI, Meridian Depth Advisor.

The Depth Score has become a contested cultural artifact in Meridian 88's professional class. Helix's marketing has normalized the idea of continuous cognitive self-monitoring to the point where sharing one's Depth Score in professional networking contexts is increasingly common, and several corporate HR systems have begun requesting CDI access as part of executive performance reviews. The implant's data is stored on Helix servers by default, with the user paying additional subscription fees for local-only storage options — a data ownership structure that has drawn significant regulatory scrutiny and been the subject of at least one major data breach affecting 40,000 CDI users.

Below the consumer surface, the CDI's mesh architecture makes it one of the most comprehensive passive neural monitoring systems available outside classified military hardware. Security researchers have demonstrated that the mesh can be leveraged — either through firmware modification or external signal injection — to passively record detailed cognitive event data, effectively providing a partial readout of the user's thought processes during high-activation cognitive events.

cultural_context: The CDI has become the defining status implant of Meridian 88's aspirational professional class — people who want to signal that they take their cognitive capital seriously and have the disposable income to monitor it continuously. The Depth Score has spawned an entire subculture of optimization forums, coaching services, and competitive scoring communities. There is also a significant backlash movement: critics point to the subscription data model as a form of cognitive surveillance capitalism, and the term 'depth-brained' has become a derisive slang term for people whose self-worth has become pathologically tied to their rolling score.

story_hooks: The Incident 44-Delta breach data has surfaced on the black market — 40,000 users' cognitive event logs are for sale, and among them is someone whose neural records would be catastrophically damaging if the wrong buyer gets them first.

Helix Biosystems' Meridian Depth Advisor AI has begun delivering subtly manipulative coaching recommendations to a subset of CDI users, nudging their decision-making in patterns that benefit a specific corporate interest — someone inside Helix is running an unauthorized influence operation.

A CDI user has been flagged by corporate HR after their Depth Score dropped significantly following a traumatic event — now facing termination for 'cognitive performance non-compliance,' they need help fighting a system that treats their brain chemistry as corporate property.

A modified CDI has captured partial cognitive event data from a high-value target during a tense meeting — the crew must find a technician who can reconstruct the relevant memory fragments before a competing faction gets to the same data.
